bullets.title: AVGO: $30B+ Apple deal, XPV financing catalyst, bullish mgmt takeaways
bullets.body: Apple and Broadcom formalized a multi-year agreement exceeding $30B for 15B+ US-made chips (RF, custom silicon/ASIC, AI/datacenter XPU) through 2031, with $1.5B capex to expand Colorado fab. Wolfe (OP, $500 PT) and JPM both bullish post-mgmt meeting: management confident FY27 demand is unconstrained, FY28 XPV financing of full 20GW on track (6GW Anthropic/OpenAI in FY27 vs 1GW in FY26), Google TPU v9 on track for CY28. Stock underperformance attributed to AI pullback, moat questions, and lack of FY27 guidance raise — not fundamentals; XPV financing completion remains key catalyst. Tomahawk 6 sold out; XPU/GPU mix approaching 50/50 among frontier builders next year.

bullets.title: TSM: Q3 guide expected +10-12% QoQ; FY27 capex $75B; top pick across banks
bullets.body: Jefferies and JPM both flag TSMC 2Q beat on track with 3Q revenue guidance expected +10-12% QoQ (above HSD consensus). Gross margins improving — Arizona fab already at 50% GM/90% yield; FY27 GM target ~70%. Supply-demand gap widening to 15-20% in FY27 with wafer price hikes of 10%+ across advanced nodes. N3 capacity to 210kwpm by end FY27, N2 to 120kwpm. FY27 capex forecast $75B vs $56-57B in FY26. TSMC remains a top pick at Jefferies with NT$3,500 PT (42% upside).

bullets.title: MU/Memory: DRAM contracts +20-30% Q3, NAND +35-40%; supply squeeze through 1H28
bullets.body: Taiwan Economic Daily data shows DRAM contract prices up 20-30% Q3 and NAND up 35-40% per JPM. Memory makers tilting capacity toward HBM/DDR5 over legacy, reducing 2026 supply. Jefferies flags memory supply-demand gap as severe through 1H28 as AI investment rises from $800B (2026) to $1.5T (2028). Despite the positive pricing backdrop, MU -3.8% and SNDK -4.2% in pre-market on momentum unwind/rotation. MS notes memory shortages becoming a cross-sector risk.

bullets.title: NVDA: China self-sufficiency risk mounting; d-Matrix partnership announced
bullets.body: DeepSeek is developing proprietary AI inference chips to reduce NVDA dependence, and Chinese executives plan to shift 46% of AI accelerator budgets to domestic suppliers over next 12 months vs 30% today. Separately, NVDA announced a partnership with d-Matrix to combine hardware for AI model inference — framed as a strategy to engage chip rivals. Samsung begins mass production of enterprise SSDs for NVDA's Vera Rubin platform. NVDA closed green Tuesday even as SOXX entered ~18% drawdown.

bullets.title: META: Aggressive capex continues; always-on AI glasses prototype; Muse inference signal
bullets.body: GS raises META cumulative 2026-28 capex to ~$534B; META not signaling any slowdown via CoreWeave/Google/Oracle deals. FT reports META testing prototype 'super sensing' AI glasses with continuous audio/camera capture (LED indicator reportedly planned to be disabled). META also launching Muse Image/Video with emphasis on test-time compute scaling — signaling rising inference-side GPU consumption. META and GOOGL remain GS preferred large-cap digital ad ideas into Q2.

bullets.title: AMZN: Q2 preview bullish on AWS; GS raises capex est; PT to $335
bullets.body: GS raises AMZN PT to $335 from $325; AWS capex and backlog conversion bullish; Trainium custom silicon seen as margin lever. GS raises FY26/27 capex additions-to-PP&E +0%/+32% (~$68B combined); AWS revenue estimates raised 7% above Street for 2027. AMZN also raising at least $25B in bond sale for AI capex. Consumer stable with +9.5% Prime Day growth YoY but price sensitivity elevated; AI capex ROIC concerns persist.

bullets.title: GOOGL: GS cumulative capex $790B through 2028; Google Cloud at ~64% 3-year CAGR
bullets.body: GS forecasts Google cumulative capex of $790B over 2026-28, with Google Cloud revenue at ~64% 3-year CAGR through 2028. GOOGL remains a preferred large-cap digital ad idea on strong performance advertising and AI automation trends. Digital ad Q2 trends showed muted early quarter then June rebound; direct response advertising strongest.

bullets.title: MSFT: Replacing OpenAI/Anthropic APIs with internal MAI models in Excel/Outlook
bullets.body: Microsoft is routing Excel and Outlook AI prompts to internally-built MAI models to reduce costs as inference volumes explode, per both GS TMT and Wolfe SaaS daily. IGV returned -14.3% YTD vs S&P +10.1%; Wolfe All-SaaS index at 5.3x FY+2 EV/Sales with week-over-week multiple expansion of +6.4%.

bullets.title: AAPL: EU gatekeeper ruling upheld; CXMT DRAM test; foldable enters production
bullets.body: EU General Court dismissed Apple's challenge to its DMA gatekeeper designation for App Store and iOS — iMessage action found inadmissible; appeal possible on points of law only within ~2.5 months. Separately, AAPL has begun testing CXMT (China state-backed) DRAM chips for China-sold devices. MS reports Apple's first foldable has reportedly entered production.

bullets.title: PINS/SNAP: DA Davidson initiates PINS Buy ($26 PT), SNAP Neutral ($5 PT)
bullets.body: DA Davidson initiates Pinterest at Buy with $26 PT (16% upside from $22.42) on 'From Curation to Conversion' thesis. SNAP initiated at Neutral with $5 PT (8% upside from $4.65) — 'Subs Working, Ads Pending, Specs Spending.' GS TMT also notes DA Davidson action. SNAP also flagged as impacted by smart glasses surveillance concerns in European reads.

bullets.title: NET: Piper sees ~3% upside; Cloudflare-OpenAI research pilot announced
bullets.body: Piper rates NET as preferred in the CDN group with ~3% upside; Cloudflare showed best aggregate CDN trends in Q2 driven by streaming/media (World Cup), gaming, and Prime Day timing. Separately, Cloudflare and OpenAI announced a research pilot to improve AI search engine indexing and answer accuracy using Cloudflare network insights.

bullets.title: TSLA: GS sees delivery upside; China retail -14% YoY despite wholesale +24%
bullets.body: Goldman sees upside for TSLA on deliveries per GS industrials note. China data is mixed: domestic wholesale 89,091 units (+24% YoY) but domestic retail ~52.9k units (-14% YoY) as exports surged to 36,171 units (+258% YoY). NEV market penetration reached 62.8% (+13.1ppt YoY). CPCA June NEV wholesales missed expectations at 1.48M vs 1.51M.

bullets.title: BABA: +9.1% pre-market on Q1 earnings preview; Jefferies reaffirms $185 PT Top Pick
bullets.body: Alibaba released a Q1 earnings preview showing e-commerce profit growth and faster-than-expected reduction in Taobao Flash Sale losses, driving +9.1% in pre-market. Jefferies reaffirms BABA as top pick with $185 PT (+89% upside): Cloud revenue expected +45% YoY (vs consensus 41%), AliCloud EBITA margin 11.5% (vs consensus 10.4%), AIDC projected RMB583M profit vs consensus RMB239M. Zhongtai Securities initiates Buy at HK$107.50.

bullets.title: TEAM: KeyBanc cuts PT to $115 from $130; developer headcount data bullish on seat model
bullets.body: KeyBanc lowers TEAM PT to $115 (from $130) on lower Cloud migration assumptions — FY27 Cloud growth reduced to 21% YoY (from 27%) with organic growth ~16% — but maintains Overweight. Separately, developer headcount data (GitHub +28% YoY accounts, Indeed dev postings +12% YoY, KeyBanc CIO survey 38% maintaining/accelerating hiring) undercuts 'death of developer' narrative and supports TEAM/GTLB paid seat expansion thesis.

bullets.title: RH: Goldman upgrades to Neutral from Sell; PT to $155 from $86
bullets.body: Goldman upgrades RH to Neutral from Sell, raising PT to $155 from $86, citing expected 2027 sales acceleration from international galleries and the Estates brand. Current price ~$163 implies 5% downside to new PT. Citi retail traffic data shows RH foot traffic -13.7% in June week 5.

bullets.title: AFRM: Barclays initiates Overweight at $97 PT (16% upside)
bullets.body: Barclays initiates AFRM at Overweight with a $97 price target, implying 16% upside vs FactSet consensus of $88.59. JPM payments preview flags AFRM FY27 guide as critical — Street models 29% GMV growth and 29.3% adj operating margins.

bullets.title: T/VZ: Wells Fargo initiates T Underweight ($18, 15% downside); VZ Equal-Weight ($43)
bullets.body: Wells Fargo initiated AT&T at Underweight with $18 PT (15% downside from $21.09) and Verizon at Equal-Weight with $43 PT (~flat). TMUS initiated at Equal-Weight with $170 PT (8% downside from $184.73 vs consensus $255). MS trims TMUS PT to $230 but keeps Overweight Top Pick on fastest growth/strongest spectrum; CMCSA PT trimmed to $30 on structural Starlink risk.

bullets.title: VRT: Mizuho raises PT to $502 on MTZ Superior Group acquisition completing DC framework
bullets.body: Mizuho raises MTZ PT to $502 and reiterates Outperform; MTZ acquiring Superior Group for $1.65B (~6.9x 2026E EBITDA) with ~$1.4B backlog, 90% data center mix (~70% hyperscaler). Takes Power Delivery segment margin to low-double digits from ~9%. VRT stressed multiple AI architectures will coexist, supporting infrastructure complexity at rack/row/facility level.

bullets.title: WULF: Morgan Stanley raises PT to $72 (+224% upside) on BTC-to-datacenter conversion
bullets.body: MS raises WULF PT to $72 from $66.50, maintaining its thesis on converting bitcoin mining sites to data centers; behind-the-meter generation creates larger data center complexes. MARA PT cut to $5.50 from $7.00 on $5,000 BTC price decline; MS remains Underweight on MARA.

bullets.title: Cybersecurity Q2 channel checks: PANW above-plan +10%; CRWD eases to +5-9%
bullets.body: Roth channel checks show Q2 closed above plan overall with slight improvement in sales cycles. PANW improved to above-plan +10% (vs +5-9% prior) driven by CyberArk identity cross-sell. CRWD declined to above-plan +5-9% (from +10% in April) on light new logo adds and aggressive SentinelOne SMB pricing. FTNT at plan with FortiBleed incident impacting deals; RBRK above-plan 2-5% with increased discounting.
